answer: One extra fake identity costs $300: a $60 chip plus a $240 bond, because a fresh fingerprint unlocks only one chip, and a farm cannot split one bond across fifty accounts. A scanner records the fingerprint ridge pattern on the chip, never sending the raw print out. The chip makes its own key, which cannot be copied to forge a second identity, and the agent locks $240 in escrow under that key. The network checks both before the agent draws any nectar from the pool, and slashes the bond on a repeat fingerprint or chip. It is like a beekeeper who must buy a new hive for every new colony.
